heard: A spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid, it couldn't close its lid. In 2020, NASA cameras captured a terrifying sight. The mission's prehistoric sample was escaping into space. To understand the leak, we must look at the collection attempt on asteroid Bennu. OSIRIS-Rx used a burst of nitrogen gas to stir up surface rocks for collection. But the collector worked too well, pulling in large pebbles that jammed the seal wide open. Fearing a total loss, engineers scrapped mass measurements and rushed to lock the sample away. When the capsule landed in Utah in 2023, the team recovered 121.6 grams of material. This accidental bounty held the building blocks of life, which is why the spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid.
